absent: Locking discipline and concurrency rules for capability tables, performance registers, timer state and random sources are not shown.
Memory layout, size and field offsets of firmware result, capability descriptor, atomic and counter data structures are not shown.
Boot sequencing, exception handling flow and overflow interrupt handling beyond register access are not shown.
Counter widths, overflow periods and admissibility of event codes are not shown.
End-to-end error handling for firmware transport failures beyond negative status is not shown.
Ordering guarantees of barriers after cluster writes beyond presence of a barrier are not shown.

findings.text: The timer layer exposes readers for physical and virtual counters that return a 64 bit tick value after applying architected ordering enforcement. A stable virtual counter variant uses a torn-read resistant register path before the same ordering step.

Timer initialization on this architecture always reports success with no work. A separate setter records event-stream support in the CPU feature store and, when compatibility support is present, in the compat capability mask, while a query reports whether that named feature is present.

Firmware true random support is probed through the version service and accepted only for non-negative results at or above the minimum level. Hardware random availability distinguishes finalized state from early boot, consulting the local CPU descriptor when not finalized and non-preemptible, otherwise consulting the patched global view. An early helper detects the random extension directly from the instruction-set feature register.

The generic random interface yields at most one word per call from the live random register when the caller requests a positive length and the system-wide capability is present. The seed interface prefers the firmware random service for up to three words on success, mapping successive result slots into the caller buffer, and otherwise falls back to one word from the reseeded register when available.

Both special register readers convey success through processor condition state produced by the read, converted to a boolean outcome. Zero-length requests always produce zero, and failure of every backing source also produces zero rather than partial data.
The minimum accepted firmware true random interface version is one in the major field with zero minor, expressed as hexadecimal one followed by four zeroes.
The platform query for secure interconnect access unconditionally reports absence, so callers must assume only non-secure access.

Cluster performance registers share op0 three, op1 zero and CRn fifteen, with CRm five covering control, enable set and clear, overflow set and clear, selector and interrupt set and clear in op2 zero through seven, and CRm six covering cycle count, event type and value, mode and two capability identifiers in op2 zero through five.

Cluster counter access follows a select-then-operate discipline where indexed event value, event type and counter value operations first program the selector and then touch the shared selected-counter register, with a barrier after each write. Enabling, disabling and interrupt masking act per index through single-bit writes, and control and cycle registers are accessed directly.
Per-counter event value and event type accessors dispatch on the numeric counter identifier through a generated switch, returning zero or performing no action for out-of-range identifiers.

The core performance unit exposes direct readers and writers for control, selector, cycle count, instruction count, enable set and clear, interrupt set and clear, cycle and instruction filters, overflow clear, user enable, access control and two capability identifiers, each mapped to its dedicated system register.

PMU version is extracted as an unsigned field from the debug feature register and a separate debug register indicates instruction counter presence. Implementation is considered absent for the implementation-defined and not-implemented encodings, while point-release predicates test greater-or-equal against the four, five and nine thresholds. Module identification is read from the aliased identification register.

System-wide finalization is reported through the always-system capability in its likely-present form. A local-CPU capability query warns and fails when called preemptibly or with an out-of-range index, returns false when no descriptor is registered, and otherwise delegates to the descriptor match routine in local scope.
Unsigned feature fields are extracted by shifting left then logically shifting right to isolate the requested window, with a four-bit width used when no explicit width is supplied.

Bug reporting emits a table entry containing a location reference and a flags half-word into a dedicated section, followed by a break instruction, with alignment preserved around the entry. Verbose support stores the file name in a mergeable string section plus offset and line, while non-verbose builds omit location data entirely. A stringified form allows the same entry to be composed inside assembler string contexts for warnings.

Fault fixup categories are numbered zero through five meaning none, packet filter, user fault with error and zeroing, kernel fault with error and zeroing, user copy, and unaligned load with zero padding.

Fixup data words pack two five-bit register numbers, with the first slot starting at bit zero and the second at bit five, used either as error and zero destinations or as data and address operands. A separate single-bit flag marks user copy fixups that correspond to writes.

Raw entries record instruction and fixup offsets relative to the entry plus type and data half-words in a dedicated section. Convenience constructors build user-fault entries that encode error and zero registers, defaulting either or both to the zero register when the caller does not need them.

Checked user-access sequences label the faultable instruction and attach an exception entry that redirects to a caller-supplied fixup label, with a copy variant that additionally records whether the access is a write.

Assembly helpers provide big-endian-only inclusion with a little-endian empty counterpart, emission of a kprobe blacklist quad word naming a symbol, and a no-operation placeholder for kasan-disabled symbol export.

Note type five carries AArch64 feature properties where the AND mask uses the top two bits set and the branch-target and pointer-authentication features occupy bit zero and bit one, with the default set enabling both.

Thirty-two and sixty-four bit atomics expose plain updates, fetching variants and returning variants across relaxed, acquire, release and full orderings for logical and arithmetic updates, plus a conditional sixty-four bit decrement that only proceeds for positive values.

Each atomic operation selects at run time between the large-system-extension implementation and the load-linked store-conditional implementation based on whether the corresponding CPU capability is likely present.

Misuse hazards include querying local capabilities while preemptible which warns and yields false, requesting an unsupported cluster capability index which fails the build, addressing an unimplemented performance counter which silently yields zero or ignores the write, and relying on hardware random before system-wide detection which the interfaces deliberately refuse to support.
The generic kernel random and seed entry points are implemented inline for this architecture, allowing early use once capabilities are known without requiring an out-of-line call.

Cluster overflow handling follows a capture then clear discipline where the pending set is read, the same set is written back to clear, a barrier is issued, and the captured value is returned to the caller.
Several headers use a conventional once-only guard definition that marks the header as included to prevent repeated processing, with no behavioural effect beyond idempotent inclusion.
